analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/developer/test.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds documentation for GLM5Next tests: GLM5NextLogprobsTests, MTP logprob capture tests, NativeOutputControlRefusalTests, verifiedDigestExistsOnlyAfterEveryManifestFileVerified, GLM5NextProviderLoopTests, VerifiedWeightHashStoreTests, RegistrationWeightHashTests, and a note that scripts/run-provider-tests.sh points DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE at an isolated state directory (head lines 117-143).

No executable code, workflow, protocol, key handling, authorization or cache behavior is changed, so there is no new attack surface and no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011 or the T-041 cache threat. The T-041 cache posture (HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, KEK purge) is untouched.

The documentation is security-adjacent in two places. The first is the weight-hash claim, which states that the load reports the manifest aggregate only after every file verified and that a same-size corrupted shard leaves it unset. This relates to A-004, T-012 and T-027. It is a description of test expectations only; I did not verify the underlying implementation, which is outside the supplied evidence. The second is the logprobs tests, which describe the relay channel receiving logprob entries per token. This is consistent with the existing statement that only the coordinator relay emits logprobs. The text does not describe plaintext leakage, and encryption behavior (T-008) is not affected.

The remainder of the file (base lines 489-1098 and head lines 1-478) is unchanged context. Test instructions use isolated state, synthetic credentials and loopback, and state they must not stop an operator process, which is consistent with the stated assumptions. The patch excerpt is truncated at one point, but the changed-range map is complete and lists only the ranges above. The accompanying source and test changes that these docs reference are not in this batch; their correctness is not evaluated here.
